facts.statement: The species Parvodus graciliani was named by Ribeiro & França.
Parvodus graciliani lived in the Late Jurassic.
The type locality of Parvodus graciliani is the Aliança Formation in Brazil.
Parvodus graciliani belongs to the order Hybodontiformes and the family Lonchidiidae.
facts.quote: Notes: A member of Hybodontiformes belonging to the family Lonchidiidae.

facts.statement: Parvodus is an extinct genus of hybodont sharks that lived during the Mesozoic era.
facts.quote: Parvodus is an extinct genus of hybodont, known from the Mesozoic era.

facts.statement: Parvodus graciliani was named in honor of Brazilian writer Graciliano Ramos (1892–1953).
facts.quote: honoring the Brazilian writer Graciliano Ramos (1892–1953)

facts.statement: Parvodus graciliani is known from isolated teeth recovered from lacustrine deposits of the Aliança Formation.
The Aliança Formation consists of oxygenated lake deposits that hosted a diverse fauna, including hybodont sharks.
The discovery of Parvodus graciliani expands the known distribution of Parvodus into the Upper Jurassic of South America.

rejected.statement: Parvodus graciliani was described as a new species in 2026.
Parvodus graciliani is the first formally named species of the genus from the Aliança Formation.
